endings.description:
The light beyond the Stag Door annihilated the flesh that once was mine, but what remains of me is inescapable, unwounded, and beyond reproach. I ascended under The Colonel's command, my victory and the enemy's defeat guiding my path. In cobalt blue, I saw my arch enemy descend with the lamps of black nephrite, while her broken body helped me climb higher. By The Colonel's instruments and means, I rose further. I have become a Name of him. This is my calling, and mine alone; I will no longer flee. The Colonel's other Names hailed me like a comrade. Together we serve as an agitation for the study of strife, to design the course of history. Thus I now exist within the scheming of things—within the rhythm of the march, within the chain of command, within the movement of armies, within the great oppositions. When I last looked back upon the achievements of my mortal life, the enemy had already melted like ice crystals. My arch enemy, fallen to the No Where, seemed still to gaze upward with her single eye. The last shred of pity that never existed faded away. I am war, and war is me.

[Congratulations on achieving one of the major victory endings. Even a minor victory is achieved by perhaps only one in twenty players—and those who ascend this far are even fewer. We, and Janus, salute you.]

endings.label: Face in the Fire
endings.description: In 1943, we ascended in Stalingrad. Von Helling would say it was a draw, but to my mind, the German defeat was catastrophic. We were battered and bruised, just like our homeland and our army. I could anticipate her every move, and I doubt anyone else understood my strategy better than she did. The Colonel vouched for us, inviting us to ride that dreadful chariot, for we possessed cunning, iron discipline, authority, and defiance—and above all, our enmity was unyielding unto death. I and I.v.H. were excellent officers; we grew stronger, unstoppable. We commanded the toughest mortals, clashing under the iron law of steel. Now, I exist within her commands, and she lives within my tactics. It has been a long time since those unfamiliar days; we know each other, from body to strategy. Perhaps one day she will tear me apart, or I will kill her—or perhaps the fire of strife will burn us both to ashes. I think that would be sad. I think I like my place in the struggle. I think I love being edges of the same sword with her. Happy Maslenitsa. Burn a scarecrow for me." —"Conversation with the Great Steadfast One," St. Michael's Church, Spring 1948

endings.label: Blade in the Fire
endings.description: Funny thing, I received a letter from my arch enemy the other day. Beyond the usual hatred, she also mentioned old times. We fought the first time we met, and ever since, she's had to compete with me in everything. Of course, I enjoy it. Back then I had many things to worry about: the integrity of my skin, the state, the family, the end of everything... My ancestors were Tragulari, and my parents raised me in a Junker style. In such circumstances, one tends to think too much. Fortunately, things have improved greatly since Stalingrad. The Chiliarch granted me the supreme duty—to wage eternal war against my arch enemy, so other responsibilities became less important. I must say I like it. I still miss Stalingrad, and I believe Duffoure would have liked it too (may The Colonel bless him). At that time the Empire's army was in retreat; we received unrealistic orders, the front was too long, and the vanguard was too deep. Undoubtedly our forces would be driven out, and I was not at all surprised that the Empire lost that battle. Everything was burning then—the city, the tanks, the people... I was there, and her face emerged from the smoke and fire. We knew each other's moves by heart, even if we could not see each other clearly. I always instigated our duels and then tried every means to get the upper hand, even though I had long since passed the age of rivalry. I have seen the end of eternity and seriously considered the possibility of embracing it. For one who has been to Vienna, such an end is mercy. I told myself that if the day ever came when I could no longer kindle the flame, I should seek that final conclusion. Fortunately, each time she answered me with an even more explosive flame, and I in turn wished to give her a fiercer contest. Luckily, at Stalingrad, she answered me, and I overcame her. After that, she will use infinite time to take revenge on me, until all that is seen turns to nothing. —Conversation with the Stalwart Hunter, St. Andrew's Chapel, Spring 1948

endings.label: Old Spring Days
endings.description: After the war, I went to her country, saw her city, stood before her unmarked grave, and spoke words she would never hear. I am a Soviet soldier; my duty was to defend my homeland and destroy its enemies. Perhaps this is what war is. It makes you kill people you do not wish to kill, and then it makes you spend the rest of your life remembering them. When the war is over, only the living have the right to remember. And what they remember often has nothing to do with victory." —1960, a Soviet war hero, German Democratic Republic, Berlin

endings.label: The Accused
endings.description: "I once thought war was the cruelest thing. Then I experienced peace. I was arrested. For collaboration and a host of fabricated charges. Did it really matter? I was the Union's weapon, and weapons are not meant to do anything else. The struggle was no longer pure. After my release, I did not return to Stalingrad—now it is Volgograd. I went to a place where no one knew me, where no one knew whom I had killed, where no one knew I had fought Germans, where no one knew I had been in Lubyanka, where no one knew I had spent ten years in Vorkuta. No one knew her either. No one knew my story with her. Perhaps this is how it ends. This story will be buried, buried in the snows of Siberia." —An accused collaborator, 1972, Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Siberia

endings.label: Victory and Survival
endings.description: "I left the country that gave me birth and raised me, not because I hated it, but because there were no more battlefields there. At least not the kind I understood. Some say love is war. I do not know if I ever loved, but I cannot live without war. The Perseus Company took me to many places. We had all sorts of people; it reminded me of the old days—very, very old days. So old that I had not even met that person yet. We never spoke again, of course, because I killed her. Perhaps one day a bullet will send me to that place, and I will tell her: I killed you, and then I lived for decades using what you taught me. I am a soldier, not a saint. I have not forgiven myself, and I have not forgotten you. I just never stopped moving." —A mercenary, 1957, French Republic, Paris

endings.label: Martyr of the Contest
endings.description: "She was born in a dead country and died in the ruins of another country about to die. I buried her bones where she fell. There was nothing there, except a blade that had once been hers—nothing else. It was my gift, but I had no right to keep it. We were taught: struggle needs fuel, victory needs sacrifice, and sacrifice never asks whether it is worth it. She died by my hand, before the counteroffensive. When I lose this war, when I escape the Führerbunker in Berlin, when I am burned to ash by incendiary bombs—I will go to the other side of the contest to find you. Then, I will be your promised offering." —Diary of a German officer found in the ruins, Greater German Reich, Berlin, April 1945
